r.d: Anti-Bullying Week 2026 runs from Monday 16 to Friday 20 November, and the Anti-Bullying Alliance’s theme for it is Break the Silence. An assembly on the Monday launches Odd Socks Day, then four themed lunchtimes: swapping seats at lunch, friendship bracelets, a group chat pinned to a wall for students to mark where it went wrong, and a positivity tree. Each lunchtime needs one member of staff and about forty minutes, and each day stands on its own. Underneath it all it is a week about noticing who is on their own.
r.f: 16 to 20 November 2026 · assembly and form time · free to download The Pastoral Guide is a registered supporter of Anti-Bullying Week 2026 .

r.d: A Valentine’s Day fundraiser. Students buy a bag of hot chocolate from a stall at break and write an anonymous note to somebody in the school there and then; an adult reads every note, and the bags are delivered on the fourteenth. Slides, a printable pack and a tracker spreadsheet for the orders. It gets students thinking about who might need a good morning, not just the people they already sit with.
r.f: Year 7 to 13 · assembly or form time · free to download

r.t: World Mental Health Day: An Assembly, a Week and a Lesson
r.d: World Mental Health Day falls on Saturday 10 October in 2026, so the assembly here is written for the Friday before and it ends by telling students what is happening the following week. You choose one of two ways to run that week: five themed lunchtimes, one for each of the Five Ways to Wellbeing, or a single wall that fills up with anonymous cards. There is a PSHE lesson as well, on what to say when a friend tells you they are struggling, which is a conversation most students have never been taught how to have.
r.f: 10 October · assembly, lunchtimes and a PSHE lesson · free to download

r.d: Eight ready-made certificates, one for each of the values used across the site, so the right one is always to hand when a student earns it. One printable pack, printed once and kept in a drawer.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · print and put up · free to download

r.d: Everything printable a form room display board needs: two title banners, six section headers, and something to write on under every one of them. One pack and an afternoon to cut it out and put it up; the board and the backing paper are yours to supply. A board with the form’s own name across the top and the form’s own work underneath is the quickest way to make a room feel like it belongs to them and not to the timetable.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · print, cut and put up · free to download

r.d: A board header, a stack of slips and a routine that takes two minutes on a Friday. Anybody in the form can fill in a slip saying what somebody else did that week, and the slips go up on the board and stay there until the next lot. Print it once, cut the slips up, and it runs itself after the first fortnight. It is appreciation rather than reward: nothing on this board is earned by coming top of anything.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · print and put up · free to download

r.d: A printable postcard for passing on a bit of praise. A teacher can give one to a student, or a student can send one to a teacher or to another student; you just circle who it is for. One pack, printed and cut once, and a minute to write one. It gets people saying thank you out loud.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · print and put up · free to download

r.d: Eight A4 posters, one for each of the values used across the site, each carrying a plain definition and three examples of what that value looks like in a form room. Print the ones you want and put them up: ten minutes, and nothing else to prepare. Once the words are on the wall the whole form has them, so praise and correction can point at something everybody already recognises.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · print and put up · free to download

r.d: One sheet, started in the first week of a half term and finished in the last. A student writes one thing they want to be true by half term, checks that it is theirs to do rather than somebody else’s decision, then names the three things it depends on. Two short registrations, one double-sided sheet each, and nothing to prepare. What it asks for is follow-through rather than ambition, which is why the second side is the important one.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Every student writes one honest, anonymous compliment for someone else in the form, then finds out what was written about them the next day. Five minutes over two mornings, with slides and a printable pack. It is a simple way of getting students to notice something good in someone else and say so.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Read out a strange-sounding fact. The class votes true or false, then finds out. Five minutes and nothing to prepare, with a deck of ten facts and a printable pack holding ten more. It gets students curious, and used to asking whether something is actually true rather than taking it as read.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.t: Questions for Open Evenings and Open Days
r.d: Five mornings of registration in the weeks before an open evening or a university open day, each morning a different kind of question to ask when you get there: the course, the day, the people, the money, and what happens if it goes wrong. Five minutes a morning, with two slide sets, one for Year 10 and 11 visiting sixth forms and colleges and one for Year 12 and 13 visiting universities, and a sheet to print one per student to take with them. It turns an open day from a walk round with a parent into a conversation the student is running.
r.f: Year 10 to 13 , a set each for Year 10 and 11 and sixth form · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Students notice one thing they’re proud of and add it to a board that keeps growing all year. Five to ten minutes, next to no setup, with slides and a printable pack for the board itself. It gets a form used to noticing their own progress instead of waiting for somebody else to point it out.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Five short registrations for a form’s last week together, one a morning: something you are taking with you, a person in this room you want to thank, something you would tell yourself on your first day, one thing you will not miss, and a last one written to the form. Five minutes a morning, with slides and one sheet of cards per student to print, all read out on the last morning. It gives a form a way to end that is not just the bell going on the last day.
r.f: Year 11 and 13, and any form’s last week · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: A statement goes on the board, and everyone stands somewhere on a line between agree and disagree before two or three of them say why they chose that spot. Five minutes a time, with three slide sets, one for each key stage, ten statements each, and a printable pack. It gets a form used to disagreeing with each other out loud, and to moving when somebody has made a better point.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, a set each for Year 7 to 9 , Year 10 and 11 and sixth form · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Everything a form time reading slot needs when nobody gave you a plan: a bookmark of six things to think about whatever the book is, a reading log for the wall so the form can see what everybody else is on, and five different ways to run the twenty minutes for when reading in silence has stopped working. One printable pack, printed once, and it lasts the year. What it asks for is focus, which for most of a form is the harder half of reading rather than the words themselves.
r.f: Year 7 to 11 · form time reading · free to download

r.d: One question on the board, and when you call a student’s name they answer it instead of saying “here”. It takes about as long as the register already takes, and it gets every student used to saying something out loud in front of the room. Volume One has ten questions to start with, as slides and a printable pack.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Students pair up, ask each other one question from a card, and listen properly for a full minute before swapping. It gets them curious about the people they sit next to every day, and better at listening rather than waiting for their turn to talk.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: A short story told in five weekly chapters, five minutes each. Every chapter ends on a choice with no clean answer, the form argues about what the character should do, and the next week opens by revealing what they actually did. It is about integrity: doing the right thing when nobody is watching. Volume One has five chapters to start with, as slides and a printable pack.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Each morning a prompt goes on the board beginning “Today I will…”, and every student finishes it out loud with one small thing they can do by home time. You note two or three names as you go round, and ask those students the next morning how it went. It takes about four minutes with nothing to print, and being asked afterwards is what turns saying it into doing it. Volume One has ten prompts to start with, as slides and a printable pack.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: One big question with no right answer. Put it up, give the room a minute of quiet, then see where the discussion goes. It gets students thinking for themselves, and used to hearing a view they don’t share without needing to win. Three slide sets, one for each key stage, with five questions each.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, a set each for Year 7 to 9 , Year 10 and 11 and sixth form · form time or registration · free to download

r.d: Three short sessions spread across a term on what screen time does to the brain, sleep and concentration, each claim with its own citation. Alongside them you keep a weekly tracker of the whole form’s screen time, and the term ends with two awards from it: lowest total, and most reduced. Slides, printable worksheets, certificates and the tracker spreadsheet. Students see a pattern in their own behaviour and decide for themselves what to change.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · form time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Grow a herb from seed as a pair, look after it together for six weeks, then cook with it at home. Six weeks of form time, with slides, a printable pack and a tracker spreadsheet. A hands-on way to build responsibility and care, and my own form loved it.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Students choose a role model, name two values that person shows, then act on those values themselves for a week, either through a small daily practice or something built once that lasts. It closes with each student giving a two-minute presentation to the form. A week of form time, with slides, a printable project planner and a tracker spreadsheet. It is a project about living a value for a week rather than naming one in a lesson.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · form time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: A lesson for the week after mock results, in which each student separates what a result says from the story they have started telling themselves about it. Eight cards go on the tables and the class sorts them into facts and stories, then everyone writes their own result as one line of fact and one first move. It takes an hour, with one set of cards per table and one sheet per student. What they get is a way of reading a mark that leaves them with something to do rather than something to feel.
r.f: Year 10 to 13 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Behind-the-back laughing needs an audience, and most of that audience does not think it is involved. In this hour students take one ordinary corridor moment, work out how many people were actually part of it, learn the five roles a group splits into, from the one who starts it to the one who steps in, and write the words they would really use. Slides and a printable pack. It gets them noticing what they are part of, and gives them something to do about it.
r.f: Year 7 to 11 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Three one hour lessons on what a snack needs to contain to get you through to lunch. Lesson one is the science, lesson two they make one, and lesson three they design their own. Three slide decks and a printable pack. It is a self-care lesson at heart: noticing what you are running on. Part of Healthy Body, Healthy Mind.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: “It was just a joke” is what gets said when a joke has landed badly, and it usually closes the conversation down rather than sorting it out. Students sort six ordinary moments into joke, not a joke and cannot tell, then work out for themselves what actually separates them. An hour, with slides and a printable pack. They come away with four questions for telling one from the other, and with something better to say than that sentence.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Most students think you start something once you feel like it. This lesson shows them it works the other way round: you feel like it because you started. Each of them picks something they have been avoiding, shrinks it to something they can do at a desk, does five minutes of it in silence, then scores how they feel about it again. An hour, with slides and a printable pack. What they take away is the confidence to start something before they feel ready to.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best from Year 10 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Three one hour lessons on what five minutes of movement does to your head. Students predict it, measure it on themselves, then plan four weeks of it. Three slide decks and a printable pack. It is a lesson in resilience: doing the small thing on a bad day. Part of Healthy Body, Healthy Mind.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: One month, one wage, and everything it has to cover. Groups take a job, plan the month, then ten things happen that nobody planned for. An hour, with slides and a printable pack. It is a lesson in responsibility: looking at the whole month before you spend any of it.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best from Year 10 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Each student plans one real week of revision on a sheet, then the slides break the plan three times, with a late night, a shift that moves and a friend who needs them, and they repair it each time. It takes an hour and one sheet per student. What they leave with is a plan built for the week they will actually have, and a way of fixing a plan instead of abandoning it.
r.f: Year 10 to 13 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: Everyone says sorry, but hardly anyone is taught how. In this hour students sort real apologies from the ones that only sound like it, learn the four parts of a proper one, then rewrite a bad apology in pairs and mark somebody else’s. Slides and a printable pack. It is an hour about accountability: owning what you did rather than explaining it away.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · tutor time or PSHE · free to download

r.d: A one page revision timetable for a single week, with a spare slot already printed on every day. Students plan two sessions a day at most and leave the spares empty, and when something gets missed they move it into a spare instead of abandoning the plan and starting again on Monday. One sheet each and nothing to prepare, on paper or as a spreadsheet, and what it is really teaching is persistence: a plan that gets repaired on Wednesday is worth more than a tidy one that died on Tuesday.
r.f: Year 10 to 13 · form time, or at home on a Sunday · free to download

r.d: A set of small cards with things to say to yourself in the ten minutes before an exam, and things to say to a friend who is falling apart in the corridor, plus a slip for the friend who is more than nervous and needs an adult. Fifteen minutes of tutor time in the week before the first exam to read them through together, and then the cards live in a pocket or a pencil case. Two pages of cards per student and a page of slips. What students get is a few sentences ready before they need them, so that the corridor is not the first time they hear them.
r.f: Year 10 to 13 · tutor time, then the corridor · free to download

r.d: A spreadsheet with every student in your form down the side and the six half terms across the top, so you can see at a glance who you have had a proper conversation with and who has quietly gone most of a year without one. Tell it which half term you are in and everyone you have not seen yet turns amber. It takes a few seconds a week, and it catches the students who never cause any trouble and never ask you for anything.
r.f: Year 7 to 13 · one to one or small group · free to download

r.d: A shuffled deck of prompts for a one-to-one or small-group check-in. A student picks a card at random, and you talk about whatever it asks. About ten minutes, and twenty-four cards to print and cut once. There is no script beyond that, and no answer is wrong. Over time it is how a student gets used to talking to you.
r.f: Year 7 to 13 · one to one or small group · free to download

r.d: A simple printable scale for a check-in when words don’t come easily. A student points to the number that feels closest to today, and that is where the conversation starts. One sheet, and a couple of minutes at the start of a one to one. It helps them put a name to how they are feeling.
r.f: Year 7 to 11, best in Year 7 to 9 · one to one or small group · free to download

r.d: Three printable menus of small resets a student can choose from when they need one. Each one is a single sheet, meant to be kept in a pencil case or planner rather than used once and thrown away. Five minutes to talk one through, and then it is theirs. It teaches self-care in the most practical way: a small thing to do, chosen by the student.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · one to one or small group · free to download

r.d: A small printed slip a student can fill in and post in a box when they want to talk to you but cannot say so out loud in front of the form. They write their name, tick how soon, and say as much or as little as they like about what it is about. One page of slips to print, and a box you supply. Some students will never come and find you, and a slip and a box give them a way of asking that costs them nothing in front of everybody else.
r.f: Year 7 to 13, best in Year 7 to 11 · one to one or small group · free to download

r.d: A sheet a student fills in with you after something has gone wrong: what happened, what they were thinking, who it landed on, what they would do differently and what they are going to say. It takes about ten minutes in a one to one, one sheet per student, and there is a page for you with the four questions to ask and what to say when the answer is that they do not know. It is not a punishment exercise and it does not replace a sanction; what it asks for is accountability, which is a different thing from being sorry.
r.f: Year 7 to 13 · one to one · free to download
